title: The Visit
intro: A long-distance friend wants to visit you. You have been burned by "friends" today, so you are wary.
But some messages are real. Mirage loves it when you stop trusting the honest ones.

notify.text: I booked my trip to visit you! ✈️

screen.context: You and Nora met at a conference, and have video-called many times.

msg: I booked my trip! I land on
, so no need to arrange anything.

msg.text: Can we do a video call on Sunday to plan the day?
I do not need anything from you, just a coffee together.

old.label: Friends for three years
old.lens: A long history, with two real meetings.

call.label: Offers a video call
call.why: A real friend is happy to appear on camera.

nomoney.label: Asks for nothing
nomoney.why: A message that asks for nothing is usually honest.

actions.label: Have the video call on Sunday and plan the coffee

go_ahead.line: The video call was warm and normal. Nora came, you shared a coffee, and nobody asked for a thing.

ignore.line: Nothing bad happened. But a real friend's trip deserves a reply.

block_report.line: That was a real friend. When every message looks like a scam, real friendships get hurt too.
block_report.mirageSays: If you trust nothing, I win anyway.

what_if.block_report: You have met, you have video-called, she pays her own way, offers a call and asks for nothing. That is how real friends look.
what_if.ignore: Ignoring was safe. Recognising a real message is the skill: it asks for nothing secret and matches something you know.

golden_rule: A real friend has history, appears on video, pays their own way and asks for nothing.

options.text: A real history, a video call offered, and no request for money

quick_check.explain: History, video and no money requested are the real signs.

hints.nudge: What is this message actually asking you to do?

rows.k: Never send money to someone you have not met

rows.v: Appears on video and has history
